To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of a SAW microfluidic mixing system to enhance chemiluminescence detection in a microfluidic flow injection analysis system leads to a theoretical limit of 0.2 nL of l-proline (a decade improvement over the gold-standard and two order of magnitude more sensitive) and that this system is portable.
we have developed a microfluidic mixing technique that can be used in a flow-injection analysis (FIA) system to enhance detection of chemiluminscent species.

(1) we developed a microfluidic platform for the detection of a chemically generated luminescence species, (2) the platform was used for the detection of l-proline, a common amino acid, and (3) we demonstrated that the limit of detection of the platform can be improved by two orders of magnitude compared to that of a conventional system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of microfluidics-based technologies for the rapid and sensitive quantification of chemical species in the aquatic environment.
the development of microfluidics-based technologies for the analysis of complex environmental samples.
the development of microfluidic technologies for the miniaturization of chemical analytical systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work represents a significant advance in the miniaturization of flow injection systems for environmental analysis, and it provides an excellent platform for the future development of a completely integrated portable microfluidic analytical system.

we demonstrate the use an integrated acousto-fluidic system to enhance the chemilumescence detection limit of a widely used reagent, and thus the sensitivity of the analysis, by two orders of magnitude.

this paper demonstrates that microfluidic mixing can be used to improve detection limits in a portable chemiluminescence system, and this is a step forward in the miniaturization of analytical systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of microfluidic mixing can enhance the detection limit of a common chemiluminscent reagent to a theoretical limit of 0.2 n M.

this study demonstrates that the combination of microfluidic actuating and mixing schemes, with the integration of a portable photodetection system, can be used to achieve a complete miniaturization of a flow injection analysis system.

the use of microfluidic mixing to enhance the sensitivity of a chemiluminiscence-based analytical method can lead to a portable analytical system with a theoretical limit of 0.2 nMs, which is a 10-fold improvement over the current industry standard and 2 orders of magnitude more than that of conventional systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microfluidic mixing is not limited to the microfluidic realm, and can be used to improve the performance of conventional analytical systems.
the use of microfluidic mixing schemes can significantly enhance the sensitivity of on-chip analytical systems and thus facilitate their use for field-based applications.

the integration of microfluidic mixing with microscale detection can be used to enhance the detection sensitivity of a given analyte, which can be used to reduce sample preconcentration steps and/or improve the limit of detection of the analytical system.
